contentText: Syllabus (GS3):  Banking - loan types, NPA, SARFAESI, IBC, DICGC, Bad Bank, PCA, BASEL-III, RBI dividend. 1. Loan Types Q - Secured vs Unsecured loans? Secured loan Unsecured (collateral-free) loan Asset pledged (home, gold, auto, FD/shares) No collateral (overdraft, credit card, personal, student, farmer loans) Lower risk -> lower interest, higher amount, longer tenure Higher risk -> higher interest, lower amount, shorter tenure  Exception: education/MSME/farmer loans are unsecured but cheap due to Govt credit guarantee Q - Fixed vs Floating interest loans? Fixed interest loan Floating interest loan Rate fixed for whole tenure (e.g. 7% crop loans up to Rs.3 lakh) External Benchmark + spread + risk premium; benchmark updated so rate moves  Teaser loan = floating sub-type: low early rate, higher later. Caused US subprime crisis (2007-08); RBI regulates (not banned) since 2011 Borrower types: Prime:  can repay. Subprime (individual):  cannot repay; teaser home loans to them caused US subprime crisis -> Global Financial Crisis (GFC). Overleveraged (company):  borrowed more than it can repay (high Debt-to-Equity). Zombie lending:  a weak bank keeps lending to a subprime/overleveraged borrower. Impaired loan:  not being repaid per original terms. Other:  Only RBI can set credit-card interest rates (SC 2024, Banking Regulation Act 1949 - consumer courts can't). Non-financial debt = housing loans, credit-card dues, T-bills. Syndicated lending spreads default risk across many lenders. Q - Twin Balance Sheet (TBS) problem - 3 stages (ES 2015-16)? Till mid-2000s: global boom; Indian corporates over-borrowed (over-leveraged). From 2007-08: subprime + GFC; exports fell; policy paralysis + judicial/environment activism delayed projects. By 2013: ~1/3rd of bank loans held by 'IC1' firms (Interest Coverage Ratio < 1 = can't even pay loan interest). Result: weak balance sheets of both big corporates AND public sector banks = Twin Balance Sheet Syndrome. 2. NPA & Classifications NPA  = loan where principal/interest unpaid for >90 days from due date. For farm loans, counted by cropping seasons (not days). Q - Loan asset classification (as it worsens)? Classification Meaning Standard Asset Repaid on time. SMA-0 / SMA-1 / SMA-2 Special Mention Account: unpaid 1-30 / 31-60 / 61-90 days. Substandard asset In NPA for 12 months or more. Doubtful asset In substandard for 12 months or more. Loss asset Little/no recoverable value (declared by bank/auditor/RBI). Gross NPA (GNPA):  total of all NPA loans;  Net NPA  = GNPA - provisioning. Provisioning:  funds set aside for potential loan losses (separate from CRR/SLR). Formula shifts to Expected Credit Loss (ECL) from 2027 (was 'incurred loss'). Loan write-off:  removing loan from asset side (tax benefit); does NOT waive recovery right; lowers reported NPA%. Restructured loan:  principal/rate/tenure modified.  Stressed assets  = NPA + written-off + restructured. Evergreening:  new loan taken to repay an old loan.  OTS with haircut:  one-time settlement where bank forgoes part of dues. ES24/ES25:  NPA fell due to loan recovery + write-offs. Credit-to-GDP gap positive/high = crisis looming; India's bank-credit-to-GDP is lower than US/UK/Japan (sustainable). 3. SARFAESI Act 2002 Narsimham-I -> Debt Recovery Tribunals (DRT, 1993); Narsimham-II ->  SARFAESI Act 2002 . Lenders can attach/auction mortgaged assets, change board, sell to Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARC) - WITHOUT going to ordinary courts. NOT applicable to farm loans. Appeal path:  DRT -> DRAT (needs 50% dues deposited) -> High Court. Who has SARFAESI power:  all banks (commercial + cooperative), Housing Finance Companies, and NBFCs IF asset size >= Rs.100 cr AND loan >= Rs.20 lakh. Defaulter rights:  60-day notice before auction, right to be heard, fair-value auction, return of surplus proceeds, humane recovery (agents only 7am-7pm). Limitations:  DRTs/DRATs understaffed (cases drag), asset value erodes, auction may not fetch best price - so IBC (arbitration) was added. 4. Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code (IBC) 2016 Q - Financial vs Operational creditors? Financial Creditors (FC) Operational Creditors (OC) Banks, NBFCs, bondholders, home buyers Suppliers, contractors, employees (dues pending) Can sit in the Committee of Creditors (CoC) Cannot sit in the CoC Q - Appeal structure (borrower type)? Individual / partnership firm Company Adjudicating authority: DRT Adjudicating authority: NCLT Appeal: NCLAT -> Supreme Court Appeal: NCLAT -> Supreme Court Resolution process:  an Insolvency Professional (IP) drafts a resolution plan (cut rate/extend tenure/find investor) -> presents to Committee of Creditors (CoC, FCs vote by loan share) -> if enough FCs approve it runs, else assets are liquidated. IBC recovered ~Rs.3.3-3.6 lakh cr (1000+ companies). IBC statutory body Founding law NCLT & NCLAT (Delhi) Companies Act 2013 Insolvency & Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI, Delhi) IBC 2016 (under Ministry of Corporate Affairs) Q - Insolvent vs Wilful defaulter? Insolvent (incapable) defaulter Wilful defaulter Cannot repay due to genuine shortage of money CAN repay but deliberately does not May get IBC loan restructuring Cannot contest elections / hold public office (as sought) Wilful defaulter - RBI's 6 traits:  won't pay despite means; siphons funds A->B; didn't use loan for stated asset (or sold it); removed collateral secretly; falsified records; fraudulent transactions. Data:  15,778 wilful defaulters, Rs.3.4 lakh cr (Dec 2022). RBI: declare within 6 months of NPA; compromise settlement allowed (2023). Guarantor:  as liable as the defaulter; bank can attach guarantor's accounts/property; guarantor's credit score drops. IBBI:  statutory (Min. Corporate Affairs); 10 members; chairman 5 yr; selects Insolvency Professional Agencies - ICAI, ICSI, Institute of Cost Accountants. Information Utility:  NeSL (2017, 1st) keeps borrower database.  IICA  runs a Graduate Insolvency Programme (register as IP without 10-yr experience). IBC 2020 Ordinance:  min. default for a case raised Rs.1 lakh -> Rs.1 crore (spares small businesses). ES25 on IBC:  borrowers now buy more forex hedging; bond credit spreads narrowed; reduced need for costly bank bailouts. 5. Credit Monitoring, Fugitive Offenders & DICGC Credit-info portal What it does CRILC (RBI) Central Repository of Info on Large Credits - loans above Rs.5 cr; banks submit weekly. NFIR (Budget-2023) National Financial Information Registry - 360-degree view of a borrower (with RBI). Public-Tech Platform / ULI (2023-24) 'Frictionless credit' - faster loan approval; run by RBIH, Bengaluru. eBkray/IBAPI, Baanknet e-auction portals for banks' attached properties. CEIB Unified Search (2024) Background check of large borrowers (> Rs.50 cr); with SBI. LEI (Legal Entity Identifier) 20-char global 'Aadhaar' for companies; from G20/FSB; mandatory for cross-border txns >= Rs.50 cr. Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018:  for offenders (fraud/scam >= Rs.100 cr) who flee India; PMLA special courts; if not back in 6 weeks -> declared fugitive; Indian + overseas + benami property attached; appeal only to HC/SC. Look Out Circulars:  issued by MHA's Bureau of Immigration; Bombay HC ruled banks CANNOT request LOCs against defaulters (right to travel). CARIN (2024):  India's ED joined the Camden Asset Recovery Inter-Agency Network (50+ nations). Q - DICGC Act 1961? What:  Deposit Insurance & Credit Guarantee Corp; 100% RBI-owned (Dy. Governor chairs); all banks must insure deposits. Cover:  up to Rs.5 lakh per depositor (raised from Rs.1 lakh in 2021); payout within 90 days of RBI moratorium; premium ~12 paise per Rs.100. Not covered:  NBFCs, PACS. Above Rs.5 lakh -> wait for liquidation. 2025 proposal: risk-based premium (riskier banks pay more). History:  UTI losses (2002) not covered (not a bank); FSLRC/Justice Srikrishna proposed a Resolution Corp via FRDI Bill (2017) - withdrawn 2018. 6. Bad Bank, PCA & BASEL-III Q - Bad Bank (2021)? NARCL (ARC) IDRCL (AMC) National Asset Reconstruction Company Ltd India Debt Resolution Company Ltd Buys bad loans from banks; 51% public sector banks Manages/values/auctions those assets; 51% private banks/NBFCs Prompt Corrective Action (PCA):  RBI classifies banks into risk thresholds 1/2/3 by capital & asset quality; restricts dividends/salaries/branch expansion/lending, can force merger/shutdown. It's a qualitative 'Direct Action' tool. Extended to NBFCs (2022; deposit-taking + govt NBFCs like PFC/REC; not HFCs/non-deposit NBFCs). UCBs have a 4-tier framework (by deposit size). Digital lending (2022):  RBI regulates Loan Service Providers (fintechs); FLDG (First Loss Default Guarantee) - fintech covers some bank loss; RBI publishes approved-app repository (2024). BASEL-III:  by Bank for Intl Settlements (BIS, Basel, Switzerland; 60 central banks); norms 1988(I)/2004(II)/2011(III). India phased in from 2013. Key ratios:  banks compute Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA); keep CRAR (Capital to RWA) >= 9%; plus buffers CCB, CCCB, LR, NSFR, LCR, HQLA. Higher NPA -> higher RWA -> need more capital. 2023:  RBI raised CRAR/risk-weights on unsecured loans -> banks lend more cautiously, loans dearer (up to +4%), lower bank profit. AT1 bonds:  perpetual (no maturity); on big losses can be written off or converted to shares ('Bail-In') - in news via Yes Bank. D-SIB (too big to fail):  RBI names them yearly, needs extra capital. India's 3: SBI, ICICI, HDFC. Basel Convention (distractor):  a separate treaty on transboundary movement of hazardous waste - NOT the banking norm. 7. Recapitalization, Governance & Shadow Banking PSB recapitalization:  Indradhanush plan (Rs.70,000 cr, 2015-18); Bank Recapitalization Bonds (~7%, non-transferable, non-convertible); weak banks merged (associate banks into SBI 2017; Vijaya+Dena into BoB 2019); Budget-2022 onwards no capital given (PSBs self-fund). Governance:  Gyan Sangam (2015) split PSB CMD into Chairman + MD&CEO; Bank Board Bureau (BBB, 2016, non-statutory) selected PSB/PSU-insurer heads -> replaced by FSIB (2022) after Delhi HC ruling. EASE Agenda (2018):  6-pillar PSB reform (customer responsiveness, responsible banking, credit off-take, MSME via Udyamimitra, financial inclusion, HR). Staff Accountability Framework (2022):  protects PSB managers from CBI/CVC/CAG harassment for bonafide loans (up to Rs.50 cr) that turn NPA. B.P. Kanungo (2022):  Bancassurance (bank sells insurance - legal), Cross-selling (extra products - legal), Mis-selling (misleading customer - illegal). Shadow banking (NBFCs, ES20):  operate partly outside RBI regulation; raise funds via bank loans, Commercial Papers, bonds. 3 segments: HFCs (e.g. DHFL), Liquid Debt Mutual Funds, Retail-NBFCs.  IL&FS crisis (2019)  (systemically important NBFC) triggered the NBFC liquidity crisis. Partial Credit Guarantee Scheme 2.0 = Govt covers 20% of PSB loss on NBFC/MFI debt. PNB-Nirav Modi scam:  PNB manager issued Letters of Undertaking (LoU) via SWIFT (not linked to CBS) for ~Rs.12,000 cr without collateral; Nirav/Mehul fled (2018).  Yes Bank (2025):  RBI let Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Bank take it over (AT1-bond/loan-fraud losses). 8. RBI Dividend, Reserves & Economic Capital Framework RBI income sources RBI allocates funds to Interest on G-Sec / foreign bonds / loans to banks Staff/retirement funds, bad-loan provisions, depreciation Revaluation of forex & gold reserves Contingency reserve (~Rs.2.5 lakh cr) Seigniorage (profit from printing money); penalties on banks Currency & Gold Revaluation Reserve (~Rs.7 lakh cr) Leftover profit -> paid to Govt as  dividend  (RBI Act Sec 47).  Bimal Jalan panel (2018-19)  set the Economic Capital Framework so RBI can transfer more surplus; RBI gave a record Rs.2.1 lakh cr dividend (2023-24); RBI shifted its financial year to Apr-Mar (from 2021). Section 7 & Urjit Patel:  Sec 7(1) lets Govt consult the Governor in public interest; Sec 7(2) lets Govt issue binding directions. First-ever Sec 7(1) consultation began Oct-2018 (over PCA, BASEL deadline, dividend); Governor Urjit Patel resigned Dec-2018. DICGC 100% RBI-owned; insures deposits up to Rs.5 lakh; not NBFCs. Bad Bank (2021) NARCL (buys) + IDRCL (manages). BASEL-III BIS Basel; CRAR >= 9% of RWA; D-SIBs = SBI, ICICI, HDFC. Twin Balance Sheet Weak corporate + PSB balance sheets (ES 2015-16). BBB -> FSIB (2022) Selects heads of PSBs/PSU insurers; non-statutory.
